title: Ignorance with(out) Grasping
summary: In this work, we argue that ignorance can be inherently understood as a hyperintensional notion. When faced with two logically or necessarily equivalent propositions, an agent may be ignorant of one while not of the other. To capture formally this intuition, we employ a topic-sensitive semantics, enabling the modeling of an agent's attitude toward the content of a proposition.
